description: Abstract In this article we present both the discrete and the integral form of Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz ( CBS \rm CBS ) inequality, some important generalizations in the n n -dimensional Euclidean space and in linear subspaces of it, as well as the strengthened CBS \rm CBS . The last CBS \rm CBS inequality plays an important role in elasticity problems.

title: Convolutional Neural Network based Decoders for Surface Codes
creator: Simone Bordoni, Stefano Giagu
description: Abstract The decoding of error syndromes of surface codes with classical algorithms may slow down quantum computation. To overcome this problem it is possible to implement decoding algorithms based on artificial neural networks. This work reports a study of decoders based on convolutional neural networks, tested on different code distances and noise models.

title: Transfer learning for galaxy feature detection: Finding Giant Star-forming Clumps in low redshift galaxies using Faster R-CNN
creator: Jürgen J. Popp, 1 Hugh Dickinson, 1 Stephen Serjeant, 1 Mike Walmsley, 2 Dominic Adams, 3 Lucy Fortson, 3 \newauthor Kameswara Mantha, 3 Vihang Mehta, 4 James M. Dawson, 5 Sandor Kruk 6 and Brooke Simmons 7 1 School of Physical Sciences, The Open University, Milton Keynes, MK7 6AA, UK 2 Jodrell Bank
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jürgen J. Popp, 1 Hugh Dickinson, 1 Stephen Serjeant, 1 Mike Walmsley, 2 Dominic Adams, 3 Lucy Fortson, 3 \newauthor Kameswara Mantha, 3 Vihang Mehta, 4 James M. Dawson, 5 Sandor Kruk 6 and Brooke Simmons 7 1 School of Physical Sciences, The Open University, Milton Keynes, MK7 6AA, UK 2 Jodrell Bank.

title: Gravitational wave double copy of radiation from gluon shockwave collisions
creator: Himanshu Raj, Raju Venugopalan

title: Aubry-Mather theory for contact Hamiltonian systems III
creator: Panrui Ni and Lin Wang
description: Abstract . By exploiting the contact Hamiltonian dynamics ( T ∗ ​ M × ℝ , Φ t ) (T^{*}M\times\mathbb{R},\Phi_{t}) around the Aubry set of contact Hamiltonian systems, we provide a relation among the Mather set, the Φ t \Phi_{t} -recurrent set, the strongly static set, the Aubry set, the Mañé set and the Φ t \Phi_{t} -non-wandering set.

title: Functorial splitting of l \displaystyle l -adic cohomology of an extension of group varieties
creator: Victor de Vries
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Victor de Vries. In this document we consider an exact sequence of group varieties e → N → G → Q → \displaystyle e\to N\to G\to Q\to e \displaystyle e over an algebraically closed field.

title: Task-Parameterized Imitation Learning with Time-Sensitive Constraints
creator: Julian Richter, João Oliveira, Christian Scheurer, Jochen Steil, Niels Dehio
description: Abstract Programming a robot manipulator should be as intuitive as possible. To achieve that, the paradigm of teaching motion skills by providing few demonstrations has become widely popular in recent years. Probabilistic versions thereof take into account the uncertainty given by the distribution of the training data.

title: The Hadamard gate cannot be replaced by a resource state in universal quantum computation
creator: Benjamin D.M. Jones, Noah Linden, Paul Skrzypczyk
description: Abstract We consider models of quantum computation that involve operations performed on some fixed resourceful quantum state. Examples that fit this paradigm include magic state injection and measurement-based approaches. We introduce a framework that incorporates both of these cases and focus on the role of coherence (or superposition) in this context, as exemplified through the Hadamard gate.

title: Kandinsky 3.0 Technical Report
creator: Vladimir Arkhipkin, Andrei Filatov, Viacheslav Vasilev, Anastasia Maltseva, Said Azizov, Igor Pavlov, Julia Agafonova, Andrey Kuznetsov, Denis Dimitrov
description: Abstract We † † ∗ Corresponding authors: Andrey Kuznetsov < < kuznetsov@airi.net > > , Denis Dimitrov < < dimitrov@airi.net > > . present Kandinsky 3.0 † † ∗∗ The family of models is named after Wassily Kandinsky, the great Russian artist and an art theorist, the father of abstract art.

title: How to detect the spacetime curvature without rulers and clocks. II. Three-dimensional spacetime
creator: A. V. Nenashev, S. D. Baranovskii
description: Abstract We have generalized the results of the previous work [arXiv:2302.12209] to the case of three-dimensional (3D) spacetime with two spatial and one temporal coordinates. We have found that the flat Minkowski 3D spacetime is “well-stitched”, which means that it possesses a structure described by 24 causal relations between 12 events.

title: Defense Against Adversarial Attacks using Convolutional Auto-Encoders
creator: Shreyasi Mandal
description: Abstract Deep learning models, while achieving state-of-the-art performance on many tasks, are susceptible to adversarial attacks that exploit inherent vulnerabilities in their architectures. Adversarial attacks manipulate the input data with imperceptible perturbations, causing the model to misclassify the data or produce erroneous outputs. This work is based on enhancing the robustness of targeted classifier models against adversarial attacks.

title: Two counterexamples to a conjecture of Colin de Verdière on multiplicity
creator: Maxime Fortier Bourque, Émile Gruda-Mediavilla, Bram Petri, Mathieu Pineault
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Maxime Fortier Bourque, Émile Gruda-Mediavilla, Bram Petri, Mathieu Pineault. We exhibit closed hyperbolic surfaces of genus 10 10 and 17 17 such that the multiplicity of the first nonzero eigenvalue of their Laplacian is larger than the maximum conjectured by Yves Colin de Verdière in 1986. In order to determine these multiplicities, we apply the twisted Selberg trace formula to the representations induced by the isometry groups of these surfaces on corresponding triangle groups.

title: On boundary controllability for the higher order nonlinear Schrödinger equation Thanks: This paper has been supported by Russian Science Foundation grant 23-21-00101.
creator: Andrei V. Faminskii
description: Abstract . A control problem with final overdetermination is considered for the higher order nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a bounded interval. The boundary condition on the space derivative is chosen as the control. Results on global existence of solutions under small input date are established. 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 35Q55, 35Q53 1.

title: Towards Sobolev Pruning DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Platform for Advanced Scientific Computing Conference ; June 03–05,2024; Zurich, Switzerland CCS: Applied computing Mathematics and statistics CCS: Computing methodologies Uncertainty quantification CCS: Computing methodologies Model verificat
creator: Neil Kichler, Sher Afghan, Uwe Naumann
description: Abstract . The increasing use of stochastic models for describing complex phenomena warrants surrogate models that capture the reference model characteristics at a fraction of the computational cost, foregoing potentially expensive Monte Carlo simulation. The predominant approach of fitting a large neural network and then pruning it to a reduced size has commonly neglected shortcomings.

title: Internal and External Calculi: Ordering the Jungle without Being Lost in Translations
creator: Tim S. Lyon ORCID:0000-0003-3214-0828, Agata Ciabattoni, Didier Galmiche, Dominique Larchey-Wendling, Daniel Méry, Nicola Olivetti, Revantha Ramanayake
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tim S. Lyon ORCID:0000-0003-3214-0828, Agata Ciabattoni, Didier Galmiche, Dominique Larchey-Wendling, Daniel Méry, Nicola Olivetti, Revantha Ramanayake. This paper gives a broad account of the various sequent-based proof formalisms in the proof-theoretic literature. We consider formalisms for various modal and tense logics, intuitionistic logic, conditional logics, and bunched logics. After providing an overview of the logics and proof formalisms under consideration, we show how these sequent-based formalisms can be placed in a hierarchy in terms of the underlying data structure of the sequents.

title: FRDiff : Feature Reuse for Universal Training-free Acceleration of Diffusion Models
creator: Junhyuk So, Jungwon Lee, Eunhyeok Park
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Junhyuk So, Jungwon Lee, Eunhyeok Park. The substantial computational costs of diffusion models, especially due to the repeated denoising steps necessary for high-quality image generation, present a major obstacle to their widespread adoption. While several studies have attempted to address this issue by reducing the number of score function evaluations (NFE) using advanced ODE solvers without fine-tuning, the decreased number of denoising iterations misses the opportunity to update fine details, resulting in noticeable quality degradation.

title: Automorphism groups of cocompact CAT(0) cube complexes and simplicity
creator: Tobias Hartnick, Merlin Incerti–Medici
description: Abstract . We provide a systematic description of the automorphism groups of specially cocompact CAT(0) \CAT cube complexes. We show that these groups are topologically finitely generated, present a method to explicitly obtain generating sets, and prove a dichotomy on their size.

title: Sig-Networks Toolkit: Signature Networks for Longitudinal Language Modelling
creator: Talia Tseriotou, Ryan Sze-Yin Chan, Adam Tsakalidis, Iman Munire Bilal, Elena Kochkina, Terry Lyons, Maria Liakata
description: Abstract We present an open-source, pip installable toolkit, Sig-Networks , the first of its kind for longitudinal language modelling. A central focus is the incorporation of Signature-based Neural Network models, which have recently shown success in temporal tasks. We apply and extend published research providing a full suite of signature-based models.

title: Minimal slopes and bubbling for complex Hessian equations Thanks: Work supported in part by the Infosys Young Investigator award, SERB MATRICS grant MTR/2022/000260, PhD scholarship from the Indian Institute of Science, and the National Science Foundation grant DMS-2203607
creator: Ved Datar, Ramesh Mete, Jian Song
description: Abstract . The existence of smooth solutions to a broad class of complex Hessian equations is related to nonlinear Nakai type criterias on intersection numbers on Kähler manifolds. Such a Nakai criteria can be interpreted as a slope stability condition analogous to the slope stability for Hermitian vector bundles over Kähler manifolds.

title: Momentum anisotropy generation in a hybrid approach †
creator: Niklas Götz*, Lucas Constantin, Hannah Elfner
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Niklas Götz*, Lucas Constantin, Hannah Elfner. Anisotropic flow emerges in all three of hybrid approaches: initial conditions, viscous relativistic hydrodynamics as well as hadronic transport. Previous works focus mainly on a constant or temperature dependent shear viscosity η / s \eta/s . Here instead, we study qualitatively the effect of a generalized η / s ⁡ ( T , μ B ) \eta/s(T,\mu_{B}) in the hybrid approach SMASH-vHLLE-hybrid.

title: Decomposing Thermodynamic Dissipation of Linear Langevin Systems via Oscillatory Modes and Its Application to Neural Dynamics
creator: Daiki Sekizawa, Sosuke Ito, Masafumi Oizumi
description: Abstract Recent developments in stochastic thermodynamics have elucidated various relations between the entropy production rate (thermodynamic dissipation) and the physical limits of information processing in nonequilibrium dynamical systems. These findings have been actively utilized and have opened new perspectives in the analysis of real biological systems.

title: MCAIMem: a M ixed SRAM and eDRAM C ell for Area and Energy-efficient on-chip AI Mem ory Thanks: Manuscript created October, 2023; This work was developed by the Yale University. This work is distributed under the L a T e X Project Public License (LPPL) ( http://www.latex-project.org/ ) version 1.3.
creator: Duy-Thanh Nguyen, Abhiroop Bhattacharjee, Abhishek Moitra, Priyadarshini Panda
description: Abstract AI chips commonly employ SRAM memory as buffers for their reliability and speed, which contribute to high performance. However, SRAM is expensive and demands significant area and energy consumption. Previous studies have explored replacing SRAM with emerging technologies like non-volatile memory, which offers fast-read memory access and a small cell area.

title: GPT-4 Enhanced Multimodal Grounding for Autonomous Driving: Leveraging Cross-Modal Attention with Large Language Models
creator: Haicheng LiaoUniversity of MacauMacau SAR, China yc27979@um.edu.mo, Huanming Shen UESTCChengdu, China HuanmingShen@outlook.com, Zhenning Li University of MacauMacau SAR, China zhenningli@um.edu.mo Chengyue Wang University of MacauMacau SAR, China chengyuewang@um.edu.mo Guofa Li Chongqing UniversityC
description: Abstract In the field of autonomous vehicles (AVs), accurately discerning commander intent and executing linguistic commands within a visual context presents a significant challenge. This paper introduces a sophisticated encoder-decoder framework, developed to address visual grounding in AVs. Our Context-Aware Visual Grounding (CAVG) model is an advanced system that integrates five core encoders—Text, Image, Context, and Cross-Modal—with a Multimodal decoder.

title: Enabling Edge Artificial Intelligence via Goal-oriented Deep Neural Network Splitting Thanks: This work was supported by MIUR under the PRIN Liquid Edge Contract, by the ANR under the France 2030 program, grant ”NF-NAI: ANR-22-PEFT-0003”, by the European Union under the Italian National Recovery and
creator: Francesco Binucci, Mattia Merluzzi, Paolo Banelli, Emilio Calvanese Strinati, Paolo Di Lorenzo
description: Abstract Deep Neural Network (DNN) splitting is one of the key enablers of edge Artificial Intelligence (AI), as it allows end users to pre-process data and offload part of the computational burden to nearby Edge Cloud Servers (ECSs). This opens new opportunities and degrees of freedom in balancing energy consumption, delay, accuracy, privacy, and other trustworthiness metrics.

title: Reconstructed (charm) baryon methods at finite temperature on anisotropic lattices
creator: Jon-Ivar Skullerud
description: Abstract Reconstructed-correlator methods have been used to investigate thermal effects in mesonic correlation functions in a fit-independent manner. This technique has recently been extended to the baryonic sector. In this work different ways of implementing this approach for baryon correlators are examined.

title: Incorporating the algorithm for the boundary condition from FVM into the framework of Eulerian SPH
creator: Zhentong Wang, Oskar J. Haidn, Xiangyu Hu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhentong Wang, Oskar J. Haidn, Xiangyu Hu. Finite volume method (FVM) is a widely used mesh-based technique, renowned for its computational efficiency and accuracy but it bears significant drawbacks, particularly in mesh generation and handling complex boundary interfaces or conditions. On the other hand, smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method, a popular meshless alternative, inherently circumvents the mesh generation and yields smoother numerical outcomes but at the expense of computational efficiency.

title: Enhancing Kinship Verification through Multiscale Retinex and Combined Deep-Shallow features
creator: El Ouanas Belabbaci 1 , Mohammed Khammari 2 , Ammar Chouchane 3,4 , Mohcene Bessaoudi 4 , Abdelmalik Ouamane 4 , Yassine Himeur 5 , Shadi Atallal 5 and Wathiq Mansoor 5
description: Abstract The challenge of kinship verification from facial images represents a cutting-edge and formidable frontier in the realms of pattern recognition and computer vision. This area of study holds a myriad of potential applications, spanning from image annotation and forensic analysis to social media research.

title: Low-shot Object Learning with Mutual Exclusivity Bias
creator: Anh Thai, Ahmad Humayun, Stefan Stojanov, Zixuan Huang, Bikram Boote, James M. Rehg
description: Abstract This paper introduces Low-shot Object Learning with Mutual Exclusivity Bias (LSME), the first computational framing of mutual exclusivity bias, a phenomenon commonly observed in infants during word learning. We provide a novel dataset, comprehensive baselines, and a state-of-the-art method to enable the ML community to tackle this challenging learning task.

title: The first five years of the AAA algorithm
creator: Yuji Nakatsukasa (), Olivier Sète (), Lloyd N. Trefethen ()
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuji Nakatsukasa (), Olivier Sète (), Lloyd N. Trefethen (). The AAA algorithm, introduced in 2018, computes best or near-best rational approximations to functions or data on subsets of the real line or the complex plane. It is much faster and more robust than previous algorithms for such problems and has been used in many applications since its appearance, including the numerical solution of Laplace, Poisson, and biharmonic PDE problems in irregular domains.

title: Accelerated Gradient Algorithms with Adaptive Subspace Search for Instance-Faster Optimization
creator: Yuanshi Liu Peking University liu _ _ \_ yuanshi@pku.edu.cn, Hanzhen Zhao Peking University hzzhao@pku.edu.cn, Yang Xu Peking University xuyang1014@pku.edu.cn, Pengyun Yue Peking University yuepy@pku.edu.cn, Cong Fang Peking University fangcong@pku.edu.cn
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuanshi Liu Peking University liu _ _ \_ yuanshi@pku.edu.cn, Hanzhen Zhao Peking University hzzhao@pku.edu.cn, Yang Xu Peking University xuyang1014@pku.edu.cn, Pengyun Yue Peking University yuepy@pku.edu.cn, Cong Fang Peking University fangcong@pku.edu.cn. Gradient-based minimax optimal algorithms have greatly promoted the development of continuous optimization and machine learning, with the measurement of performance based on the hardest instance.

title: Characterization of weighted Hardy spaces on which all composition operators are bounded
creator: Pascal Lefèvre, Daniel Li
description: Abstract Abstract. We give a complete characterization of the sequences \beta=(\beta_{n}) of positive numbers for which all composition operators on H^{2}(\beta) are bounded, where H^{2}(\beta) is the space of analytic functions f on the unit disk \mathbb{D} such that \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}|a_{n}|^{2}\beta_{n}<+\infty if f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_{n}z^{n} .

title: XAIQA: Explainer-Based Data Augmentation for Extractive Question Answering
creator: Joel Stremmel, Ardavan Saeedi, Hamid Hassanzadeh, Sanjit Batra, Jeffrey Hertzberg, Jaime Murillo, Eran Halperin
description: Abstract Extractive question answering (QA) systems can enable physicians and researchers to query medical records, a foundational capability for designing clinical studies and understanding patient medical history. However, building these systems typically requires expert-annotated QA pairs. Large language models (LLMs), which can perform extractive QA, depend on high quality data in their prompts, specialized for the application domain.

title: Elliptic Weingarten surfaces of minimal type in ℝ 2 × h ℝ \mathbb{R}^{2}\times_{h}\mathbb{R}
creator: Carlos Peñafiel, Bernardo A. Quaglia and Haimer A. Trejos
description: Abstract . In this paper, we study the elliptic Weingarten of minimal type surfaces immersed in the warped product space ℝ 2 × h ℝ \mathbb{R}^{2}\times_{h}\mathbb{R} , when h h is a C 1 C^{1} -function in ℝ 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} with radial symmetry.

title: Fluorescence Lifetime Hong-Ou-Mandel Sensing
creator: Ashley Lyons, Vytautas Zickus, Raúl Álvarez-Mendoza, Danilo Triggiani, Vincenzo Tamma, Niclas Westerberg, Manlio Tassieri, Daniele Faccio
description: Abstract Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy in the time domain is typically performed by recording the arrival time of photons either by using electronic time tagging or a gated detector. As such the temporal resolution is limited by the performance of the electronics to 100 100 ’s of picoseconds.

title: Improving Bias Mitigation through Bias Experts in Natural Language Understanding
creator: Eojin Jeon, Mingyu Lee, Juhyeong Park, Yeachan Kim, Wing-Lam Mok, SangKeun Lee
description: Abstract Biases in the dataset often enable the model to achieve high performance on in-distribution data, while poorly performing on out-of-distribution data. To mitigate the detrimental effect of the bias on the networks, previous works have proposed debiasing methods that down-weight the biased examples identified by an auxiliary model, which is trained with explicit bias labels.

title: DocBinFormer: A Two-Level Transformer Network for Effective Document Image Binarization Thanks: R. Biswas is with Optiks Innovations Pvt. Ltd (P360), Mumbai, Maharashtra 400066, India (e-mail: risab.biswas@p360.com). Thanks: S. K. Roy is with the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Alipu
creator: Risab Biswas, Swalpa Kumar Roy, Ning Wang, Umapada Pal
description: Abstract In real life, various degradation scenarios exist that might damage document images, making it harder to recognize and analyze them, thus binarization is a fundamental and crucial step for achieving the most optimal performance in any document analysis task.

title: Revisiting Micro and Macro Expressions in Computer Graphics Characters Conference: 22nd Brazilian Symposium on Games and Digital Entertainment; November 06–09, 2023; Rio Grande (RS), Brazil 22nd Brazilian Symposium on Games and Digital Entertainment (SBGames 2023), November 06–09, 2023, Rio Grande (
creator: Rubens Montanha, Giovana Raupp, Vitoria Gonzalez, Yanny Partichelli, André Bins, Marcos Ferreira, Victor Araujo and Soraia Musse
description: Abstract . This paper presents the reproduction of two studies focused on the perception of micro and macro expressions of Virtual Humans (VHs) generated by Computer Graphics (CG), first described in 2014 and replicated in 2021. The 2014 study referred to a VH realistic, whereas, in 2021, it referred to a VH cartoon.

title: Language-Informed Visual Concept Learning
creator: Sharon Lee, Yunzhi Zhang Shangzhe WuJiajun Wu Stanford University
description: Abstract Our understanding of the visual world is centered around various concept axes, characterizing different aspects of visual entities. While different concept axes can be easily specified by language, e.g . , color , the exact visual nuances along each axis often exceed the limitations of linguistic articulations, e.g . , a particular style of painting.

title: List chromatic number of the square of a sparse random graph
creator: Alan Frieze, Aditya Raut
description: Abstract We show that w.h.p the list chromatic number χ ℓ \chi_{\ell} of the square of G n , p G_{n,p} for p = c / n p=c/n is asymptotically equal to the maximum degree Δ ⁡ ( G n , p ) \Delta(G_{n,p}) .

title: Excluded minors of interval positroids that are paving matroids
creator: Hyungju Park
description: Abstract . We prove that every paving matroid that is an excluded minor of interval positroids can be reduced to one of three fundamental families of excluded minors of interval positroids by relaxing dependent hyperplanes. Using this result, we classify all non-positroid excluded minors of interval positroids that are paving matroids.

title: A Task is Worth One Word: Learning with Task Prompts for High-Quality Versatile Image Inpainting
creator: Junhao Zhuang, Yanhong Zeng, Wenran Liu, Chun Yuan, Kai Chen
description: Abstract Achieving high-quality versatile image inpainting, where user-specified regions are filled with plausible content according to user intent, presents a significant challenge. Existing methods face difficulties in simultaneously addressing context-aware image inpainting and text-guided object inpainting due to the distinct optimal training strategies required.

title: A Mixed Integer Quadratic Program for Valuing the Impact of Price and Forecast Uncertainty for Wind Generators Thanks: The information, data, or work presented herein was supported by the National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship under Grant No. 2141064 as well as in part by the Advan
creator: Daniel Shen and Marija Ilic
description: Abstract Owners of wind power plants are exposed to financial risk in wholesale electricity markets due to the uncertain nature of wind forecasts and price volatility. In the event of a wind shortfall, the plant may have to repurchase power at a higher price in the real-time market.

title: Foundation Model Assisted Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
creator: Xiaobo Yang, Xiaojin Gong
description: Abstract This work aims to leverage pre-trained foundation models, such as contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) and segment anything model (SAM), to address weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) using image-level labels. To this end, we propose a coarse-to-fine framework based on CLIP and SAM for generating high-quality segmentation seeds.

title: Enhanced star formation and metallicity deficit in the USS 1558–003 forming protocluster at z=2.53 2022 Enhanced star formation and metallicity deficit in the USS 1558–003 forming protocluster at z=2.53 – 2
creator: J. M. Pérez-Martínez, T. Kodama, Y. Koyama, R. Shimakawa, T. L. Suzuki, K. Daikuhara, K. Adachi, M. Onodera, I. Tanaka
description: Abstract We use K-band multi-object near-infrared spectroscopy with Keck/MOSFIRE to search for environmental imprints on the gas properties of 27 narrow-band selected H α \alpha emitters (HAEs) across the three major clumps of the assembling USS1558–003 protocluster at z = 2.53 z=2.53 .

title: Physical Symbolic Optimization
creator: Wassim Tenachi, Rodrigo Ibata, Foivos I. Diakogiannis
description: Abstract We present a framework for constraining the automatic sequential generation of equations to obey the rules of dimensional analysis by construction. Combining this approach with reinforcement learning, we built Φ \Phi -SO, a Physical Symbolic Optimization method for recovering analytical functions from physical data leveraging units constraints.

title: DiffusionSat: A Generative Foundation Model for Satellite Imagery
creator: Samar Khanna, Patrick Liu, Linqi Zhou, Chenlin Meng, Robin Rombach, Marshall Burke, David B. Lobell, Stefano Ermon
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Samar Khanna, Patrick Liu, Linqi Zhou, Chenlin Meng, Robin Rombach, Marshall Burke, David B. Lobell, Stefano Ermon. Diffusion models have achieved state-of-the-art results on many modalities including images, speech, and video. However, existing models are not tailored to support remote sensing data, which is widely used in important applications including environmental monitoring and crop-yield prediction.

title: Superconductivity in the Bilayer Two-orbital Hubbard Model
creator: Yao-Yuan Zheng, Wéi Wú
description: Abstract Motivated by the recently discovered high T c T_{c} nickelate superconductor La 3 ​ Ni 2 ​ O 7 \mathrm{La_{3}Ni_{2}O_{7}} , we investigate superconductivity in a two dimensional Hubbard model on square lattice that consists of two layers of hybridizing d x 2 − y 2 d_{x^{2}-y^{2}} and d z 2 d_{z^{2}} orbitals.

title: H i Studies of Extremely Metal-Poor Dwarfs in Voids – I H i Studies of Extremely Metal-Poor Dwarfs in Voids – I – References 2023
creator: Sushma Kurapati, Simon A. Pustilnik, Evgeniya S. Egorova, Department of Astronomy, University of Cape Town, Rondenbosch 7701, South Africa
description: Abstract We present and discuss the results of the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) H i 21-cm line mapping for five isolated low-mass (M bary ∼ \sim (2–8) × \times 10 7 M☉) eXtremely Metal Poor (XMP) dwarfs [12+ log \log (O/H)=7.13-7.28], selected from the Nearby Void Galaxy (NVG) sample.

title: MMM: Generative M asked M otion M odel
creator: Ekkasit Pinyoanuntapong, Pu Wang, Minwoo Lee, Chen Chen
description: Abstract Recent advances in text-to-motion generation using diffusion and autoregressive models have shown promising results. However, these models often suffer from a trade-off between real-time performance, high fidelity, and motion editability. To address this gap, we introduce MMM, a novel yet simple motion generation paradigm based on M asked M otion M odel.

title: Criss Cross Nebula: Case study of shock regions with resolved microstructures at scales of ∼ \sim 1000 AU Facilities: MaNGA, GASS, Purple Mountain Observatory (PMO) 13.7-m millimeter telescope, 2 m telescope in Thüringer Landessternwarte Tautenburg (Germany), China Near Earth Object Survey Telescope
creator: Tao Jing, Cheng Li, Renbin Yan, Cheng Cheng, Wei Zhang, Xihan Ji, Niu Li, Jing Wang, Chaojian Wu, Haibo Yuan
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tao Jing, Cheng Li, Renbin Yan, Cheng Cheng, Wei Zhang, Xihan Ji, Niu Li, Jing Wang, Chaojian Wu, Haibo Yuan. Using integral field spectroscopy from MaNGA, we study the resolved microstructures in a shocked region in Criss Cross Nebula (CCN), with an unprecedentedly high resolution of ≲ \lesssim 1000 AU.

title: Streaming Algorithms for the k k -Submodular Cover Problem
creator: Wenqi Wang, Gregory Gutin, Yaping Mao, Donglei Du, Xiaoyan Zhang
description: Abstract Given a natural number k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 , we consider the k k -submodular cover problem ( k k -SC). The objective is to find a minimum cost subset of a ground set 𝒳 \mathcal{X} subject to the value of a k k -submodular utility function being at least a certain predetermined value τ \tau .

title: On the existence, rareness and uniqueness of quenched Hi -rich galaxies in the local Universe
creator: Xiao Li, Cheng Li, H. J. Mo, Jianhong Hu, Jing Wang, Ting Xiao
description: Abstract Using data from ALFALFA, xGASS, HI-MaNGA and the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), we identify a sample of 47 “red but Hi -rich”(RR) galaxies with NUV − r \textrm{NUV}-r > 5 ~>5 and unusually high Hi -to-stellar mass ratios.

title: Generalized Hernandez-Leclerc modules and cluster algebras Thanks: † {\dagger} Corresponding author
creator: Jingmin Guo, Bing Duan, Yanfeng Luo †
description: Abstract . We introduce generalized Hernandez-Leclerc modules over U q ​ ( 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 n + 1 ^ ) U_{q}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}}) as a generalization of Hernandez-Leclerc modules of type A, and prove that they are real and prime via monoidal categorifications of cluster algebras.

title: Post-starburst galaxies in SDSS-IV MaNGA: Two broad categories of evolutionary pathways
creator: Zhuo Cheng, Cheng Li, Niu Li, Renbin Yan, Houjun Mo
description: Abstract We study the size-mass relation (SMR) and recent star formation history (SFH) of post-starburst (PSB) galaxies in the local Universe, using spatially resolved spectroscopy from the final data release of MaNGA. Our sample includes 489 PSB galaxies: 94 cPSB galaxies with central PSB regions, 85 rPSB galaxies with ring-like PSB regions and 310 iPSB galaxies with irregular PSB regions.

title: On Data-driven Wasserstein distributionally robust Nash equilibrium problems with heterogeneous uncertainties Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE.
creator: George Pantazis, Barbara Franci, Sergio Grammatico
description: Abstract We study stochastic Nash equilibrium problems subject to heterogeneous uncertainty on the cost functions of the individual agents. In our setting, we assume no prior knowledge of the underlying probability distributions of the uncertain variables. To account for this lack of knowledge, we consider an ambiguity set around the empirical probability distribution under the Wasserstein metric.

title: Theta-Induced Diffusion on Tate Elliptic Curves over Non-Archimedean Local Fields
creator: Patrick Erik Bradley
description: Abstract . A diffusion operator on the K K -rational points of a Tate elliptic curve E q E_{q} is constructed, where K K is a non-archimedean local field, as well as an operator on the Berkovich-analytification E q a ​ n E_{q}^{an} of E q E_{q} .
